title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Ten: Past Perfect (B2) | Forbes English
description: Camp three tells the story. Camp ten tells you what had happened before the story started — the step behind the step, the thing that was already over by…

hero.h1: The camp you had already struck
hero.lede: Camp three tells the story. Camp ten tells you what had happened before the story started — the step behind the step, the thing that was already over by the time anything else began. It is the only tense on the mountain that exists purely to put two past events in order.

cards.head: The earlier of two past actions
cards.body: Two things happened; this one happened first, and the order matters.
cards.ex: "The train had left before we reached the platform."

cards.head: The reason behind a past event
cards.body: Why something in the past was the way you found it.
cards.ex: "She was furious. Someone had taken her seat."

cards.head: By a past deadline
cards.body: by or by the time sets a moment the action had already beaten.

cards.head: Reported speech
cards.body: A past simple in the original shifts back one step when you report it.
cards.ex: "I lost it." → He said he had lost it.

cards.head: The third conditional
cards.body: An unreal past — what would have happened if things had gone differently.
cards.ex: "If we had started earlier, we would have made it."

cards.head: The first time you ever did something
cards.body: With never … before and it was the first time.
cards.ex: "It was the first time I had seen a glacier."

cards.head: Wh- questions
cards.body: question word + had + subject + past participle?

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: This is the shortest chart on the mountain. Had does not change for anybody — no was and were, no third-person -s. Every difficulty in this tense is in the participle, not the auxiliary.

charts.head: The third form — where the errors live
charts.note: After had comes the participle, which for irregular verbs is not the past simple. Putting the camp-three form here is the single commonest mistake in this tense.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this tense is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: Had takes the third form, never the past simple.
Yesterday I had gone to the shop.
Yesterday I went to the shop.
With no second past event to stand behind, the past perfect has nothing to be earlier than.
She has left before I arrived.
She had left before I arrived.
Camp four measures back to now; camp ten measures back to a past moment.

charts.note: Camp three is the default past tense and always will be. Camp ten is a correction you make to it — you reach for had only when the order of two past events would otherwise be read the wrong way round.

head: Question
Past perfect
Past simple
rows:
The earlier one, already over.
"He had left."
Never — it needs a second past moment to be earlier than.
Only when you go back out of order.
Allowed, but optional — the word already gives the order.

charts.example: The pair that shows the whole difference: "When I arrived, he left" — I got there, then he walked out. "When I arrived, he had left" — he was already gone; I missed him. Same two words changed, an entirely different afternoon.

signals.head: Marks the moment you measure from

sections.example: A useful habit: find the past simple first. That is the moment you are standing on. Anything that had already happened when you got there is camp ten.

panels.head: Past simple — the main event
items: … so she stood for the whole journey.
… and then he started on the rest.

quiz.prompt: The train _____ by the time we reached the platform. (leave)
quiz.hint: Which of the two happened first?
quiz.explain: The train went first, so it takes the past perfect: had left. Reaching the platform is the moment you measure back from.

quiz.prompt: She was furious. Someone _____ her seat. (take)
quiz.hint: The reason behind a past state.
quiz.explain: The seat was taken before she was furious, so it takes the past perfect. Note the participle: taken, not took.
By + a past date sets a moment the action had already beaten, which is the past perfect. Has climbed would measure back to today instead.

quiz.prompt: "I lost the key." → He said he _____ the key. (lose)
quiz.hint: Reported speech shifts back one step.
quiz.explain: A past simple in the original becomes the past perfect when reported: he said he had lost it.

quiz.prompt: If we _____ earlier, we would have made it. (start)
quiz.explain: The third conditional takes if + past perfect, then would have + participle. It describes a past that did not happen.

quiz.prompt: By the time she reached the gate, she _____ the form. (sign)
quiz.explain: Signing was finished before she reached the gate, so it takes the past perfect: had signed.

quiz.prompt: When I arrived, he _____ . He was already on the road. (leave)
quiz.explain: Had left means he was gone before I got there. Left would mean he walked out after I arrived — a different afternoon.

quiz.prompt: They _____ anything all day, and it showed. (not / eat)
quiz.explain: Hadn't + participle: hadn't eaten. Ate is the past simple form and cannot follow had.

quiz.hint: Question order for the past perfect.
quiz.explain: Questions invert had: Had you met him? The participle of meet is met.

quiz.prompt: Yesterday I _____ to the shop for bread. (go)
quiz.hint: Is there a second past event here at all?
quiz.explain: There is no earlier past event for this to stand behind, so the past simple is the right tense. The past perfect always needs something to be earlier than.

quiz.prompt: He _____ home before the storm broke. (already / go)
quiz.hint: Already sits between the two words.
quiz.explain: Already goes between had and the participle: had already gone. The storm breaking is the moment you measure back from.

quiz.prompt: She told me she _____ the letter that morning. (write)
quiz.explain: Reported speech shifts the past back to the past perfect, and the participle of write is written.

quiz.prompt: The path was wet because it _____ all night. (rain)
quiz.hint: Which came first — the rain or the wet path?
quiz.explain: The rain came before the wet path you found, so it takes the past perfect: because it had rained.

quiz.prompt: It was the first time I _____ a glacier. (never / see)
quiz.explain: It was the first time takes the past perfect: the first time I had ever seen one. Have ever seen would measure back to today.

results: Clean run. You can hear which of two past events came first, and you only reach for had when the order needs saying.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at camp three before camp eleven.
Good first attempt. The question of whether you need had at all is the part to read again.
